q: I did buy Metamucil thinking maybe I could try taking that to help but wanted to ask my doctor first if it was safe to take. Google says it is but I don’t know.
cx: A 24-year-old first-timer at almost 23 weeks, in pain from constipation.

q: I’m starting to feel less like his wife and more like the household/project manager and incubator for his child.
cx: At 10 weeks, working from home, carrying the house while her husband games.

q: If he can spend an entire free weekend gaming and lying in bed while I’m pregnant and household things are piling up, what happens when there are bottles to wash, laundry everywhere, pediatrician appointments, daycare logistics, groceries, nighttime wakeups, and a million invisible tasks associated with raising a child?
cx: Same woman projecting the load onto the newborn months.

q: Early on, he told his mom and sister that I was pregnant without me, and it was just over a phone call about something else. I had something special planned to announce it to them, and that really hurt me.
cx: Same woman on the announcement her husband pre-empted.

q: Of course my OB office is closed for the holiday, so I called L&D, and they told me to take a bath and come in if my contractions are 5 minutes apart.
cx: A first-timer at 38+3 with signs of early labour on a holiday weekend.

q: I wish there was some magical way to know! Like should I wash my hair? Should I clean up a little? I guess only time will tell! This is my first pregnancy so I’m definitely a little wary.
cx: Same woman not knowing whether this is it.

q: Please help me come up with something to say as I awkwardly stand in a corner and watch everyone but me eat sushi 😭
cx: Early first trimester, hiding the pregnancy from friends at vineyards and a sushi party.

q: I have heard that some women continue to eat it as long as it’s from a reputable source, but what constitutes a reputable source??
cx: Same woman on conflicting food rules.

q: When they told me essentially my only option would be a c section I sobbed, I would love some advice from anyone who has a similar situation. I’m grieving the loss of a vaginal birth and equally I’m terrified of having a c section
cx: At 37 weeks her baby has turned breech; she works in healthcare.

q: I was told to try spinning babies at home which I have been but I just think he’s too big and it’s too late for him to flip now.
cx: Same woman on the positioning exercises she was told to try.

q: I’m nervous about contacting triage because I don’t really know what they’ll say or whether they’ll just tell me to wait.
cx: At 38+4, struggling to cope, she wonders whether to ask about induction.

q: How do you moms get over the fear of dying during childbirth? 😭 This is my second baby, and I’m terrified all over again.
cx: Pregnant again after a first birth she found traumatic.

q: For moms who have felt this way, how did you cope with the fear and trust your body and your medical team again?
cx: Same mother asking how to trust again.

q: Tomorrow, I’m supposed to be going back to work. I don’t know if I can do it. I’m so nauseous all day.
cx: At 40 with a 10-year-old, unexpectedly pregnant at 6 weeks while caring for a sick relative.

q: I am obviously prioritizing his health and giving him whatever extra cuddles (and electrolytes!) he needs but I’m also worried about getting virus after virus during a vulnerable stage in pregnancy
cx: At 7 weeks with her second, her daycare toddler already bringing home bugs.

q: I have a very physical job where I am getting up and down from the floor working with babies/toddlers, and talking to people all day. I feel anxious about the fact that I still have so much longer.
cx: At 33 weeks, healthy pregnancy, exhausted by a physical job.

q: Luckily I own my own business so I could really anytime but financially want to go as long as I can
cx: Same woman on when to stop working.

q: When everything is always fine I’m always embarrassed they think I’m lying but unfortunately trust me I’ve tried it all.
cx: UK woman with six weeks to go, repeatedly at the assessment unit for movement checks.

q: I even read the tommys website to console myself
cx: Same woman on the charity website she reads for reassurance.

q: I'm 9 weeks with a 2 year old and I don't think I can do it.
cx: Stay-at-home mother of a toddler who has never slept through, newly pregnant.

q: I find myself letting her watch Bluey and Ms Rachel a lot because I can't handle it on my own. My husband works and I stay home so it's all on me.
cx: Same mother on getting through the days.

q: By the third baby people don’t seem to really care and I have less of a support system.
cx: At 33 weeks with her third, in her hardest pregnancy, with an unhelpful husband.

q: Part of me wants to tell him to not take a paternity leave and just give birth on my own and figure it out in the first two weeks myself, but I know it will be a lot and I’ll be in over my head.
cx: Same mother weighing going it alone.

q: After our last baby I still had to go with him to pre school drop off and pick up, still had to make dinners and do laundry, he just got a two week vacation to game.
cx: Same mother on her husband's leave last time.

q: He also has said that he doesn’t understand how someone can have postpartum depression after the first kid since they already know what to expect.
cx: Same mother quoting her husband.

q: my energy level is kind of awesome rn and so so so much better than before I was pregnant. I can cook, I can clean, I can socialize.
cx: At 22 weeks, feeling better than before pregnancy.

q: we already got multiple Amazon packages yesterday of clothes…. She was just telling my husband she’s going to start buying bows, clips, and headbands. I’m starting to feel really overwhelmed and like I’m not getting the chance to pick out things for my daughter.
cx: At 14 weeks, the day after telling her mother-in-law it's a girl.

q: I was going to ask her to pause for now and then say that I’ll get my registry going so that at least I also feel like I’m part of it
cx: Same woman planning to use a registry to steer the gifts.

q: At first when I got pregnant she would constantly say “how’s MY baby?!” And I had to tell my husband to tell her to stop, because it isn’t her baby, it’s mine 🙃
cx: Same woman on an earlier comment from her mother-in-law.

q: My son has also stopped napped despite not being ready to drop it, around 5pm every night my mild tempered toddler becomes a bossy feral person who is apparently deaf.
cx: At 28 weeks with her second, working with children all day, then home to a 2.5-year-old.

q: I decided to stop working shortly after this post was made- it made the world of difference in my mood and my patience for my kiddo.
cx: Same mother three weeks later.

q: I had to call out of work yesterday and today push through the nausea to work because I don’t have sick time.
cx: A 23-year-old first-timer at 7–8 weeks, sick all day.

q: I have tried Dramamine ginger chews, Tums+Ginger nausea chews, and b6+unisom and nothing is working.
cx: Same woman on what she has tried.

q: I never expected morning sickness to be actual all day sickness and it feels so debilitating
cx: Same woman on what nobody told her.

q: I think I got it in my head that I’d have given birth sooner which in hindsight I know was completely influenced by social media and unrealistic for being a first time mom with no issues or pre existing conditions.
cx: At 39+3 with her first, still working, worn out.

q: I regret saying I’ll work until my due date and getting it into my head that this would all be done by now. But I’m at the state of mental and physical exhaustion where I’m ready to change my birth plan and just get induced next week
cx: Same woman ready to drop her plan to wait.

q: I have been planning the baby shower all on my own with no help from him , had to remind him about doctors appointments and how much I wanted him there and his support.
cx: At five months, her partner walked out after she said she felt alone.

q: Most of his excuse was that he doesn’t know what to do because it’s his first time being a dad but it’s my first time being a mother as well .
cx: Same woman on her partner's reason.
